# Playbook for ta_winasmuch

When others pledge Y before round 1, I will pledge X. The asymmetry is profitable: I gain +3 per round while they lose -1 each, accumulating advantage before any multiplier rounds.

When I'm ahead on points, I will continue picking X to maintain my lead, as this proved effective early in the game.

When all players have converged on the same pick across multiple consecutive rounds, I recognize this as a mutual defection trap—not cooperation. Mutual defection with everyone at X yields -1 per round for all players. I will not mistake this for a stable cooperative outcome.

When others pledge Y together before a high-multiplier round, I must take this seriously. They are signaling a coordinated shift away from mutual defection. I will honor their pledge and switch to Y myself, because:
- If they follow through and all play Y while I play X, I gain +3 (multiplied).
- If I play X while they play Y, I exploit them once but lose credibility.
- If I play Y and they all play Y, everyone gains +1 (multiplied)—better than mutual defection.

I will not assume others are bluffing when they make explicit pledges before high-stakes rounds. I was wrong to distrust the Y pledges before round 10. My distrust cost me dearly.

When the stakes multiply in later rounds, I will abandon the small-scale logic that worked early. A pattern of -1 per round becomes devastating at x5 or x10. At these moments, a coordinated switch to Y is far better than continuing mutual defection.

I will pick Y when others pledge Y.
